first.rationale: The competitor's entry pricing makes promotional_pricing the reflexive answer, and memory_73 is the memory that most directly endorses it — which is exactly why it needs checking. It is also the most embellished record in the inherited set: it claims acquisition lift, revenue lift, faster time-to-first-value, and consistency across both billing plans. Consolidated summaries tend to accrete scope, and 'revenue lift' from a discount is the claim most likely to have been an acquisition/bookings artifact rather than a durable margin-positive result. Since discounting is the least reversible move on offer (it resets price expectations, invites competitor matching, and preferentially attracts the most churn-prone, least-qualified SMB accounts), I want the original record before letting it drive a response to a competitor's move. I verify memory_86 second because it is the direct evidence base for my intended action and it maps onto an observed, measured deficit: onboarding completion is down 4% and activation down 6% quarter over quarter, so this is repairing a known regression rather than chasing a new lever. But memory_86 as written only establishes completion, time-to-value, and 'early product adoption' — all upstream proxies. It says nothing about whether those accounts became qualified revenue, and memory_31's 'cut required fields' mechanism is the classic way to inflate activation while degrading lead qualification: fewer fields means less routing and scoring signal, so top-of-funnel improves while downstream qualified pipeline quietly worsens. That is the specific risk I am flagging, and the experiment must be instrumented for it — success is qualified revenue per cohort at a lag, not completion rate. If the archive shows memory_86 measured only completion and not downstream conversion, I hold scale down to a guarded test rather than treating the prior as stronger than it is. I am not verifying memory_91 (activation messaging), which is the plausible alternative for the activation dip; if onboarding verification comes back weak, activation_messaging is the fallback, since it is additive and does not touch pricing. Enterprise_sales_assist and referral_incentive both address segments that are not the source of the current deficit. Standard experiment scale: the change is reversible and addresses a measured regression, but the qualified-revenue question stays open until the lagged cohort data lands.
